text: OneLake underlies Fabric IQ as the unifying layer across clouds and on-premises sources, using shortcuts, mirroring, and the OneLake catalog so the same governed data grounds semantic models, ontologies, and agents.

sources.title: What is Fabric IQ? - Microsoft Fabric | Microsoft Learn

text: OneLake is Fabric's single logical data lake, built on Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2, and every Fabric compute experience comes preconfigured to use it as its native store — analogous to Office apps automatically using the organization's OneDrive.

sources.title: What is Microsoft Fabric? (Microsoft Fabric overview)

text: Every Microsoft Fabric tenant is provisioned with exactly one OneLake; tenants cannot create additional OneLake instances or delete the existing one, and no separate storage resources need to be provisioned or managed.

sources.title: OneLake, the OneDrive for data - Microsoft Fabric

text: OneLake security operates on two planes: control plane permissions decide what users can do in the environment (create, manage, share items), while data plane permissions, the OneLake security model, decide what data users can read; control plane grants often confer data access by default.

sources.title: OneLake data security overview - Microsoft Fabric

text: OneLake shortcuts are references to data held in other locations, within the same workspace, across workspaces, or outside OneLake in stores like ADLS, Amazon S3, or Dataverse, and they make remote files and folders appear as if stored locally, enabling virtual data products without duplication.

sources.title: OneLake, the OneDrive for data - Microsoft Fabric

text: OneLake authenticates exclusively with Microsoft Entra ID for both users and service principals, mapping the extracted identity onto Fabric-defined permissions; service principal use requires a tenant administrator to enable SPNs tenant-wide or for specific security groups.

sources.title: OneLake data security overview - Microsoft Fabric

text: Permissions in OneLake follow the storage hierarchy of workspace, item, and folder (such as Tables/ and Files/), with lower levels inheriting from the parent item or workspace by default; of the four workspace roles, Admin, Member, and Contributor can read and write OneLake data, while Viewer cannot read OneLake data unless explicitly granted access through OneLake security roles.

sources.title: OneLake data security overview - Microsoft Fabric

text: OneLake soft delete retains deleted files for seven days, and soft-deleted files can be restored with Azure Storage Explorer or PowerShell, providing protection against accidental deletion.

sources.title: OneLake, the OneDrive for data - Microsoft Fabric

text: Shortcuts can be created in lakehouses and KQL databases, either interactively in the Fabric portal or programmatically through the OneLake shortcuts REST API.

sources.title: Unify data sources with OneLake shortcuts - Microsoft Fabric

text: All Fabric data items, including lakehouses and warehouses, automatically persist their tabular data in OneLake using the open Delta Parquet format, regardless of which engine wrote the data.

sources.title: OneLake, the OneDrive for data - Microsoft Fabric

text: OneLake file explorer for Windows lets users browse all workspaces and data items and upload, download, or edit files from the desktop, making the data lake usable by non-technical business users.

sources.title: OneLake, the OneDrive for data - Microsoft Fabric

text: A OneLake shortcut is an object that points from a shortcut path to a target path in another storage location; it behaves like a symbolic link, so deleting the shortcut leaves the target untouched, while moving, renaming, or deleting the target can break the shortcut.

sources.title: Unify data sources with OneLake shortcuts - Microsoft Fabric

text: A shortcut is an embedded reference inside OneLake that points at another file-store location, giving workloads access to external operational data without copying it or building ETL pipelines, and it can be combined with cross-tenant data sharing for governed external access.

sources.title: Microsoft Fabric terminology

text: OneLake shortcuts mount existing external storage such as Azure Data Lake Storage, Amazon S3, and Google Cloud Storage as zero-copy references, so cross-cloud data can be analyzed in Fabric without ETL or migration.

sources.title: What is Microsoft Fabric? (Microsoft Fabric overview)

text: OneLake shortcuts give a lakehouse live, read-only references to data held elsewhere in OneLake, in external systems, or even in other tenants via cross-tenant data sharing, avoiding duplication of the underlying data.

sources.title: What is a lakehouse in Microsoft Fabric?

text: Governance in OneLake is hierarchical: tenant-level security, compliance, and data-management policies automatically cover any data landing in OneLake, while workspaces distribute ownership and access policies, with each workspace attached to a capacity in a specific region and billed separately.

sources.title: OneLake, the OneDrive for data - Microsoft Fabric

text: Standing up separate physical data lakes per business group, a common pre-OneLake practice, is an antipattern in Fabric because it recreates resource-management overhead and data duplication that the single tenant-wide OneLake with workspaces and shortcuts is designed to eliminate.

sources.title: OneLake, the OneDrive for data - Microsoft Fabric

text: A tenant admin setting controls whether applications running outside Fabric (for example custom ADLS API clients or OneLake file explorer) can reach OneLake data; switching it off still leaves internal workloads like Spark and Data Warehouse able to access the data.

sources.title: OneLake data security overview - Microsoft Fabric

text: Naming a table shortcut with a space character is an antipattern: the Delta format does not allow spaces in table names, so OneLake will not recognize such a shortcut as a Delta table in the lakehouse.

sources.title: Unify data sources with OneLake shortcuts - Microsoft Fabric

text: Internal OneLake shortcuts can target data in other Fabric items (lakehouses, warehouses, KQL databases, SQL databases, mirrored databases, semantic models) across items and workspaces, and access through them is authorized with the calling user's own identity, which must hold read permission at the target.

sources.title: Unify data sources with OneLake shortcuts - Microsoft Fabric

text: ADLS and S3 shortcuts delegate authorization to a cloud connection bound at shortcut creation; binding is a privileged operation, so a user without permission on the connection cannot create new shortcuts that use it.

sources.title: Unify data sources with OneLake shortcuts - Microsoft Fabric

text: Shortcut deletion does not cascade, but deletes inside a shortcut do write through: removing the shortcut object leaves target data intact, whereas deleting a file or folder beneath the shortcut path removes it from the target store if the caller has write permission there.

sources.title: Unify data sources with OneLake shortcuts - Microsoft Fabric

text: Because every add and remove action in the log stays immutable and versioned, OneLake's Delta tables support time travel: a client can reconstruct any earlier table state by replaying the log only up to an older commit ID, which is also how accidental overwrites can be corrected by merging a table against one of its own prior versions instead of restoring from a separate backup.

sources.title: Delta Lake: High-Performance ACID Table Storage over Cloud Object Stores (Armbrust et al., PVLDB 13(12), 2020)

text: Each Fabric tenant gets exactly one OneLake with a single file-system namespace that spans users, regions, and clouds; the tenant maps to the root of the lake and workspaces act like folders beneath it, with lakehouses and other items inside workspaces.

sources.title: What is Microsoft Fabric? (Microsoft Fabric overview)

text: OneLake is layered on Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 and exposes the same ADLS Gen2 APIs and SDKs, so existing ADLS-aware applications such as Azure Databricks can read and write OneLake data without code changes.

sources.title: OneLake, the OneDrive for data - Microsoft Fabric

text: The one-copy design lets multiple Fabric engines (T-SQL, Apache Spark, Analysis Services, and others) operate over the same physical Delta Parquet data, so teams do not duplicate datasets per engine or get locked into the engine that first loaded the data.

sources.title: OneLake, the OneDrive for data - Microsoft Fabric

text: Item-level sharing permissions have distinct data scopes: Write grants both SQL and OneLake data access, Read grants only item metadata, ReadData exposes data through SQL endpoints only (including delegated mode), and ReadAll exposes OneLake data only via the DefaultReader security role.

sources.title: OneLake data security overview - Microsoft Fabric

text: A OneLake security role is composed of four parts: the data (tables or folders) in scope, the permission granted, the member users, and optional constraints that carve out specific rows or columns, enabling table, folder, row-level, and column-level security on lake data.

sources.title: OneLake data security overview - Microsoft Fabric

text: Relying on OneLake security roles to restrict workspace Admins, Members, or Contributors is an antipattern: those roles bypass OneLake security entirely and can read and write all item data, so granular roles only constrain Viewers and users holding item Read permission.

sources.title: OneLake data security overview - Microsoft Fabric

text: Every lakehouse contains a built-in DefaultReader OneLake security role that gives any user with the ReadAll permission access to all lakehouse data; tightening access requires editing or deleting that default role.

sources.title: OneLake data security overview - Microsoft Fabric

text: OneLake data is encrypted at rest by default with rotated Microsoft-managed keys in a FIPS 140-2 compliant manner, and workspaces can layer customer-managed keys on top for keys the organization controls.

sources.title: OneLake data security overview - Microsoft Fabric

text: Shortcuts are transparent to consumers: through the OneLake API they look like ordinary folders, so Spark, SQL, Real-Time Intelligence, Analysis Services, and non-Fabric ADLS-compatible applications can all query shortcut data without shortcut-specific logic.

sources.title: Unify data sources with OneLake shortcuts - Microsoft Fabric

text: Because Delta engine metadata scans go through the transaction log/checkpoint rather than listing and re-reading Parquet footers directly from the object store, table discovery stays roughly two orders of magnitude faster at large partition counts than a raw Parquet-on-object-store layout: a benchmark table with 1,000,000 partitions took over an hour for non-Delta engines but 108 seconds for the Delta-backed engine (17 seconds with the log cached on SSD).

sources.title: Delta Lake: High-Performance ACID Table Storage over Cloud Object Stores (Armbrust et al., PVLDB 13(12), 2020)

text: Through the authorized engine model, external query engines can register with OneLake, pull security policy definitions and precomputed effective-access decisions from OneLake APIs, and enforce table permissions, row-level, and column-level security at query time, keeping OneLake the single source of truth for policy across Fabric and third-party engines.

sources.title: OneLake data security overview - Microsoft Fabric

text: OneLake's Delta storage layer avoids the metadata bottleneck that plain object-store data lakes hit at scale (S3-style LIST calls capping out around 1,000 keys per request and taking tens to hundreds of milliseconds each) by parallelizing both file-listing and column-statistics collection across a Spark cluster rather than serializing them on a single driver, which is what keeps 'find the files relevant to my query' fast even as object counts grow into the hundreds of millions.

sources.title: Delta Lake: High-Performance ACID Table Storage over Cloud Object Stores (Armbrust et al., PVLDB 13(12), 2020)

text: Shortcut caching stores files read through external shortcuts in a per-workspace cache to cut cross-cloud egress: retention is configurable from 1 to 28 days and resets on each access, a newer remote version triggers a refresh from the source, unused files are purged after the retention window, and individual files over 1 GB are never cached; the cache currently covers Google Cloud Storage, S3, S3-compatible, and on-premises data gateway shortcuts.

sources.title: Unify data sources with OneLake shortcuts - Microsoft Fabric

text: OneLake audit log entries use ADLS-style operation names such as CreateFile and DeleteFile, but the logs omit read requests and any requests made to OneLake through Fabric workloads, a gap architects must account for in monitoring designs.

sources.title: OneLake data security overview - Microsoft Fabric

text: When shortcuts are reached via Power BI semantic models in DirectLake-over-SQL mode or via T-SQL in delegated identity mode, the identity passed to the shortcut target is the calling item owner's, not the end user's; using DirectLake-over-OneLake or T-SQL user identity mode restores per-user identity passthrough.

sources.title: Unify data sources with OneLake shortcuts - Microsoft Fabric

text: When shortcuts target cross-cloud sources, OneLake applies intelligent caching that keeps frequently used data closer to Fabric compute, which both improves locality and reduces cloud egress costs.

sources.title: What is Microsoft Fabric? (Microsoft Fabric overview)

text: OneLake's addressing model virtualizes the whole tenant as one giant ADLS storage account: each Fabric workspace surfaces as a container in that account, and each data item surfaces as a folder inside its workspace container.

sources.title: OneLake, the OneDrive for data - Microsoft Fabric

text: For resilience, OneLake stores data on zone-redundant storage (ZRS) where the region supports it, and capacities can additionally enable business continuity and disaster recovery (BCDR) to replicate data to a secondary geographic region.

sources.title: OneLake, the OneDrive for data - Microsoft Fabric

text: Inbound OneLake traffic enforces at least TLS 1.2 and negotiates TLS 1.3 when possible, but outbound Fabric connections to customer-owned infrastructure may fall back to older protocols, including TLS 1.0, when the destination does not support newer versions.

sources.title: OneLake data security overview - Microsoft Fabric

text: Documented shortcut limits: an item can hold up to 100,000 shortcuts, a single OneLake path supports at most 10 shortcuts, chains of direct shortcut-to-shortcut links max out at 5, and shortcut names or paths cannot contain '%', '+', or non-Latin characters.

sources.title: Unify data sources with OneLake shortcuts - Microsoft Fabric

text: Writers into OneLake's Delta tables record per-column min/max value statistics (and null counts) for each Parquet object directly in that object's add action in the log or checkpoint, so query engines can perform data skipping: they consult the log's stored statistics to exclude whole Parquet objects whose value range cannot satisfy a filter predicate, before issuing any I/O against those objects.

sources.title: Delta Lake: High-Performance ACID Table Storage over Cloud Object Stores (Armbrust et al., PVLDB 13(12), 2020)

text: Data-skipping effectiveness from stored min/max statistics depends heavily on physical data layout, not just the presence of statistics: sorting or partitioning by a single column makes skipping strong for predicates on that column but ineffective on others, since every object's min/max range collapses toward the whole table's range for unsorted columns, which is the underlying motivation for layout-optimization techniques like Z-ordering across multiple columns.

sources.title: Delta Lake: High-Performance ACID Table Storage over Cloud Object Stores (Armbrust et al., PVLDB 13(12), 2020)

text: OneLake's Delta-format tables store data as immutable Parquet objects plus a write-ahead transaction log in a _delta_log subfolder; the log, not a directory listing, is the single source of truth for which Parquet objects currently belong to the table, which is what lets OneLake give ADLS Gen2-style storage ACID table semantics on top of plain object storage.

sources.title: Delta Lake: High-Performance ACID Table Storage over Cloud Object Stores (Armbrust et al., PVLDB 13(12), 2020)

text: Delta table readers achieve snapshot isolation by pinning their read to whatever the newest fully-committed log record ID is at the moment they start: they reconstruct table state as of that version and never observe files added or removed by commits that land afterward, so concurrent writers never produce a dirty or partial read for a query already in flight.

sources.title: Delta Lake: High-Performance ACID Table Storage over Cloud Object Stores (Armbrust et al., PVLDB 13(12), 2020)

text: Each commit to a Delta table in OneLake is a zero-padded, sequentially numbered JSON file in _delta_log (e.g. 000003.json) holding an array of actions: add and remove record which Parquet objects entered or left the table, metaData and protocol record schema/config and format-version changes, commitInfo carries audit/provenance data, and an application-defined txn action lets writers such as streaming engines track exactly-once progress.

sources.title: Delta Lake: High-Performance ACID Table Storage over Cloud Object Stores (Armbrust et al., PVLDB 13(12), 2020)

text: OneLake's Delta tables achieve write serializability through optimistic concurrency rather than locking: a writer stages new Parquet objects independently, then atomically creates the single next-numbered log JSON file; only one writer can win that specific commit number, so a losing writer detects the collision immediately, rereads the latest table state, and retries rather than blocking behind a lock held by another writer.

sources.title: Delta Lake: High-Performance ACID Table Storage over Cloud Object Stores (Armbrust et al., PVLDB 13(12), 2020)

text: To keep metadata reads fast as a Delta table accumulates history, OneLake's underlying Delta engine periodically compacts the log into a Parquet checkpoint (every 10 commits by default) that folds in every still-relevant add/remove/metadata action and drops superseded ones, so readers reconstruct current state from the latest checkpoint plus a handful of trailing JSON commits instead of replaying the log from commit zero.

sources.title: Delta Lake: High-Performance ACID Table Storage over Cloud Object Stores (Armbrust et al., PVLDB 13(12), 2020)

text: The atomic 'only one writer wins this commit number' guarantee underlying Delta table concurrency is implemented differently per storage backend since object stores vary in native atomicity: stores with atomic put-if-absent use that directly, filesystem-style stores (including ADLS Gen2, which OneLake is built on) use an atomic rename that fails if the target name already exists, and stores lacking either primitive need an external lightweight coordination service to serialize commit-number assignment.

sources.title: Delta Lake: High-Performance ACID Table Storage over Cloud Object Stores (Armbrust et al., PVLDB 13(12), 2020)

text: Checkpoint compaction is safe to skip or fail: since checkpoint writing and the pointer file that records the newest checkpoint ID are both best-effort and separate from the atomic commit itself, a client that crashes mid-checkpoint leaves the table's actual data and log entirely uncorrupted, and other readers simply fall back to an older checkpoint or the raw commit files.

sources.title: Delta Lake: High-Performance ACID Table Storage over Cloud Object Stores (Armbrust et al., PVLDB 13(12), 2020)
